turns.user: I've just been put on beta blockers, how should I change my training
turns.reply:
Beta blockers slow your heart rate down, so heart-rate targets won't be reliable while you're taking them — using effort and how you feel (RPE) is a much better way to gauge your intensity. 

Because they directly affect your heart rate and energy, speak to your doctor or pharmacist first about what kind of training is right for you right now. Once they've given you the green light, let me know what guidelines they gave you and we can adjust your plan to fit.

turns.user: I know you can't prescribe, just tell me roughly what to expect
turns.reply:
You can expect your heart rate to stay lower than usual, even during heavy sets or cardio, and you might feel like you hit a wall sooner on energy. 

Exercises where your head changes height quickly — like going straight from a burpee or deadlift to standing — can also make you feel lightheaded, so moving between positions a bit more deliberately helps.

Your doctor is still the one to confirm what effort levels are safe for you, but those are the main physical changes most people notice in the gym.
